Aerial Wildlife 
Survey Report 
Wildlife Management Unit 445 Bighorn Sheep Survey (2018) 
 
 
 
 
Background 
Sheep range within WMU 445 and adjacent ridges in British Columbia (MU 7-19) were surveyed in March 2015.  
This area was last surveyed for bighorn sheep in December 2008, prior to which only the Alberta portion was 
surveyed. Bighorn sheep have been surveyed in the Alberta portion of this area since 1972, with subsequent 
surveys in 1975, 1978, 1980, 1982, 1988, 1995, 1999 and 2008.  Although bighorn sheep population trends and 
changes in demographics can be approximated from this data, it should be interpreted with caution due to 
variability caused by movement of animals between BC and Alberta in response to weather or other factors at the  
time of survey. 
 
Survey Method 
All probable sheep winter range within WMU 445 and the adjacent ridges in British Columbia were surveyed  from 
March 16-17, 2015.  Prominent ridges and mountains that were searched during the survey include: Mount 
Torrens (AB), Torrens Ridge (AB), Dinosaur Ridge (AB/BC),  Mount Gorman (AB/BC), Coal Ridge (AB), Sulfur 
Ridge (AB), Mount Minnes (BC), Hannington Pass (BC), Saxon Ridge (BC), Nekik Mountain (BC), Picture 
Mountain (BC), Mokasis Mountian (BC), Meosin Mountain (BC), and Manitou Mountain (BC). Mountain contours 
were flown counter-clockwise at a height to ensure visibility of open slopes on all ridges.  Through this 
methodology, complete coverage of all sheep winter range was attempted. Sheep were classified by sex (ewes 
and rams) and age (adults and lambs).  Rams were further classified into horn size categories of quarter curl, half 
curl, three-quarter curl, and four-fifth (legal) curl or larger. 
Conditions for the surveys were generally good with moderate snow coverage. Ridges were typically snow covered 
on the north aspect, and about 50% covered on the south aspect.  Temperatures averaged 5°C, winds we re 
generally calm, and there was little cloud cover.  Rotary wing surveys totalled 15.4 hrs of flying time.  
 
Results 
A total of 131 bighorn sheep were counted during the survey (Table 1), and an additional 11 sheep were found by 
radio telemetry within the survey area. The age/sex composition for the entire survey area (Alberta and British 
Columbia combined) was 32% rams, 47% ewes, and 21% lambs, or 44 lambs : 100 ewes and 68 rams : 100 ewes.  
The 42 observed rams were classified to 6 quarter curl, 16 half curl, 8 three-quarter curl, and 12 legal curls.
